instructions:
Read the paper below and produce a structured summary.

It matched these tracked topics; `relevance` must contain one entry per slug, stating what this paper changes for that topic:
- overthinking: Overthinking — When and why large reasoning models think more than a problem needs (or less than it needs) — the accuracy/efficiency tradeoff of reasoning length, test-time compute scaling, and methods to make a model stop, or keep going, at the right point.

Rules:
- Write in en.
- Ground every statement in the supplied material. If something is not stated,
  leave the field empty rather than inferring it.
- No marketing language. Prefer the specific number over the adjective.
- Return one JSON object matching the schema exactly. No prose around it.

concepts: string - reusable ideas this paper relies on or introduces
datasets: string - datasets, benchmarks, corpora or simulators used
output_schema.limitations: string - stated limits plus any the reader should notice
output_schema.method: string - how it works, enough for a reader to explain it
methods: string - named methods, architectures or algorithms
output_schema.one_liner: string - what the paper does, in one sentence, no hype
output_schema.problem: string - the problem it addresses and why it is open

relevance.<topic-slug>: string - why this matters for that specific topic

output_schema.results: string - headline numbers, on which benchmarks, against what

payload.title: Less Diverse, Less Safe: The Indirect But Pervasive Risk of Test-Time Scaling in Large Language Models

contributions: Introduces RefDiv, a diagnostic protocol that curtails candidate diversity within test-time-scaling generation to probe safety
Shows diversity curtailment consistently raises unsafe-output rates under test-time scaling, across strategies (MCTS, Best-of-N) and across open and proprietary models
Shows existing safety filters such as Llama-Guard fail to detect RefDiv-generated adversarial inputs
result.method: RefDiv is a diagnostic protocol that constrains candidate diversity during test-time-scaling generation (tested with Monte Carlo Tree Search and Best-of-N) across multiple open models (Qwen3, Mistral, Llama3.1, Gemma3) and proprietary systems (OpenAI o3-mini, Gemini-2.5-Pro), measuring the resulting rate of unsafe outputs and testing whether existing safety classifiers detect the resulting inputs.
result.one_liner: Shows that test-time-scaling methods such as Monte Carlo Tree Search and Best-of-N become substantially more likely to produce unsafe outputs when candidate diversity is curtailed, using a diagnostic protocol called RefDiv.
result.problem: It was unclear whether test-time scaling introduces safety vulnerabilities indirectly, through reduced diversity among candidate reasoning paths or outputs, as opposed to only through explicit adversarial prompting.

relevance.overthinking: Studies test-time-scaling methods (MCTS, Best-of-N) as its subject, but from a safety angle: curtailing candidate diversity during test-time scaling raises unsafe-output rates, often more than direct adversarial prompts, and evades existing safety filters. This is a real but safety-focused contribution to the test-time-compute-scaling side of the topic, distinct from the accuracy/efficiency reasoning-length tradeoff.

result.results: Curtailing candidate diversity, even by a modest amount, consistently increases unsafe-output rates under test-time scaling, often surpassing the effect of directly adversarial prompts; the effect generalizes across MCTS and Best-of-N and across Qwen3, Mistral, Llama3.1, Gemma3, OpenAI o3-mini and Gemini-2.5-Pro; Llama-Guard fails to detect RefDiv-generated adversarial inputs.
